newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Record Australian sugar cane output said certain.
newsitem.headline: Record Australian sugar cane output said certain.

text.p: Queensland would produce a record tonnage of sugar cane in the present season and was also expected to produce a record sugar crop, Harry Bonanno, chairman of CANEGROWERS, said on Wednesday.
Bonanno was clarifying his remarks on Tuesday at the annual general meeting of CANEGROWERS, where he said the Queensland sugar industry could set new record production in 1997/98.

It was definite that the state would produce more sugar cane this season than last season's record 37.2 million tonnes, he said. "We have more than that now," he told Reuters at the 1997 Australian Sugar Convention.
Whether sugar production would beat last year's record of 5.156 million tonnes of 94 net titre sugar remained "in the lap of the gods". "But I still think we'll get it," he said.
This was despite damage to the cane crop by cyclone Justin earlier this year.
Bonanno said industry speculation at the conference that Queensland was headed toward producing 40 million tonnes of cane and 5.3 milliion tonnes of sugar this season was "possible".
The 1997 cane crush will begin next month and run until December. Queensland produces 95 percent of Australia's sugar.
